# ripple_detection

> Detects sharp-wave ripples (150-250 Hz events in hippocampal LFP) and
> multiunit high-synchrony events, with nine published and lab detectors behind
> one calling convention. Version 2.x; calls and results differ from 1.x (see
> MIGRATING.md).

Units everywhere: time in seconds, rates in Hz, speed in cm/s, durations and
gaps in seconds. A duration that looks like milliseconds (`minimum_duration=15`)
raises and says what to pass. Thresholds are in standard deviations (SD) of
each detector's own normalized trace, so they are not comparable across
detectors.

The pipeline: filter the raw LFP to the ripple band with the rate it was
recorded at, then detect. Every detector takes `time`, its signal(s), `speed`
and `sampling_frequency` positionally, then keyword-only tunables, and returns a
pandas DataFrame with one row per event, indexed by `event_number`.

```python
from ripple_detection import Kay_ripple_detector, filter_ripple_band
from ripple_detection.simulate import simulate_session, simulate_time

time = simulate_time(45_000, 1500)  # 30 s at 1500 Hz; use your own timestamps
session = simulate_session(time, [5.0, 10.0, 15.0, 20.0, 25.0], rng=0)
filtered_lfps = filter_ripple_band(session.lfps, sampling_frequency=1500)
events = Kay_ripple_detector(
    time, filtered_lfps, session.speed, 1500, zscore_threshold=2.0, minimum_duration=0.015
)
events[["start_time", "end_time", "duration", "max_sustained_zscore"]]
```

## Detectors

Each takes `(time, <signal>, speed, sampling_frequency, **tunables)`. The signal is
ripple-band LFP of shape (n_time, n_channels) unless stated.

- `Kay_ripple_detector`: z-scored consensus of the channels' envelopes (Kay et al. 2016). Default 2 SD held for 15 ms.
- `Karlsson_ripple_detector`: each channel's envelope, per-channel events merged (Karlsson & Frank 2009). 3 SD.
- `Roumis_ripple_detector`: mean over channels of the square root of each channel's smoothed squared envelope (Frank-lab variant). 2 SD.
- `Shvartsman_ripple_detector`: per-channel events kept when at least `minimum_participating_channels` (2) channels detect them; needs 2 or more channels by default. 3 SD.
- `Yu_ripple_detector`: median of per-channel z-scored envelopes; the threshold is estimated per call from immobility noise (Yu et al. 2017). Needs immobile samples.
- `Zugaro_ripple_detector`: FMAToolbox FindRipples two-threshold rule, bounds 2 SD, peak 5 SD; events of 20-100 ms by default.
- `Long_sharp_wave_ripple_detector`: takes RAW, unfiltered LFP of shape (n_time, 2), the ripple channel then a stratum radiatum channel. Ripple-band input raises nothing and returns nonsense.
- `Carey_candidate_detector`: takes ripple-band LFP and multiunit spike counts (n_time, n_units); joint ripple and multiunit score (Carey, Tanaka & van der Meer 2019).
- `multiunit_HSE_detector`: takes multiunit spike counts (n_time, n_units), no LFP; z-scored population rate.

`DETECTORS[name].describe()` returns any detector's inputs, tunables (default,
unit, meaning) and output columns as JSON-ready data, and `get_detector(name)`
resolves a stored name.

## Rules that are easy to get wrong

- `filter_ripple_band(data, sampling_frequency)` needs the rate; there is no default.
- Tunables are keyword-only: `Kay_ripple_detector(time, lfps, speed, 1500, speed_threshold=4.0)`.
- Multiunit input is spike counts or indicators per sample (non-negative whole numbers), not a rate in Hz.
- NaN in a signal is a missing sample: nothing is computed across it, and events cut off by one are flagged in `clipped_start` / `clipped_end`. NaN in speed is an unknown speed. Do not fill gaps with zeros.
- A time range for the normalization statistics is a mask: `normalization_mask=(time >= start) & (time <= end)`.
- `speed_threshold=np.inf` turns the speed criterion off; a large finite number does not cover unknown speed.

## Migrating from 1.x

Code written for 1.x needs changes, and results differ on the same recording;
[MIGRATING.md](https://github.com/Eden-Kramer-Lab/ripple_detection/blob/master/MIGRATING.md)
is the full guide. Most 1.x calls fail with a message naming the replacement;
three changes cannot raise: the column `max_thresh` is `max_sustained_zscore`,
`simulate_LFP` draws pink noise by default where 1.x drew brown, and the event
helpers return an empty `(0, 2)` array where they returned `[]`.
